doc.title: Buster Williams interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002

title: Being fearless in the music
summary: He says the music teaches fearlessness and the need to step into new places in a long solo chorus.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Fearless. And the quicker you become fearless the easier it’s going to be for you. And that’s a realization — aah, I’ve got to be like a lion. I have to fear nothing. ‘Cause what else is going to allow you, first of all, to attempt to play something different in the thirty- second chorus of this song, after you’ve been playing behind every soloist. You can’t walk the same thing. You can’t play the same notes all the time. You’ve got to be fearless. You’ve got to step out. You’ve got to step into places that you’ve never been before.
